newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise in thin nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise in thin nervous trade.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Friday but dealers said trade was thin and nervous after Thursday's sacking of security chief Alexander Lebed.
"The week has been quite difficult. We have seen a lot of volatility," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said.

He said the large price swings were due to new investors who had stepped in after Russia received a high speculative rating last week for its first Eurobond issue, but they could be selling now on the Kremlin staff changes.
But dealers said prices rose as buying prevailed in nervous thin trading.
"The West seems to consider Lebed's sacking as a stabilising factor but activity is otherwise low," a Russian bank dealer said.
He added that any weekend political events were likely to determine price moves on Monday.
